dicas.texto: Boa observação! Se duas frações são equivalentes, elas ocupam o mesmo lugar na reta numérica. Como podemos dividir a segunda reta para encontrar esse mesmo lugar usando oitavos?
Ótimo começo! Primeiro, divida a Linha 2 em 8 partes iguais (digite 8 no campo do denominador e confirme). Depois, veja em qual marca o ponto de 1/4 cai.
Quase lá! Depois de dividir em 8 partes, conte quantas marcas até chegar ao mesmo ponto de 1/4. Está entre a primeira e a terceira marca — será a segunda?
Você está muito perto! Divida a Linha 2 em 8 partes. Agora, começando do zero, conte: 1/8, 2/8... Em qual delas você chega exatamente onde está 1/4? Digite esse número no numerador!
Pense assim: se 1 inteiro tem 4 quartos, quantos oitavos tem? E quanto é metade de um quarto em termos de oitavos?
Compare as duas retas lado a lado. Veja onde 1/4 está na Linha 1 e encontre exatamente o mesmo ponto na Linha 2 já dividida em oitavos. Conte quantas partes desde o zero até lá.
Dica visual: o ponto de 1/4 está exatamente na metade entre 0 e 1/2. Na Linha 2 com 8 partes, 1/2 é 4/8. Então, metade disso é...?
Veja: 0, depois 1/8, depois 2/8... O ponto de 1/4 está logo após a primeira marca pequena. Você já passou do zero e chegou na segunda marca — então quantos oitavos são?

interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; pergunta exibida "One fourth equals how many eighths?"; DUAS retas numéricas de 0 a 1, uma acima da outra: na Linha 1 a fração dada já está marcada pelo tutor; na Linha 2 o aluno digita em quantas partes iguais dividir (campo de denominador + confirmar) e marca o ponto da fração equivalente; à direita das retas, a igualdade entre as duas frações é mostrada em caixas: as da esquerda vêm preenchidas e, na da direita, o aluno digita o NUMERADOR (o denominador alvo já aparece); há também um seletor de comparação ("≟", "=", "≠") entre as duas frações; botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (dividir a Linha 2, marcar o ponto, digitar o numerador, comparar, concluir).

dicas.texto: A fraction less than one shows only part of one whole.
Use the denominator for the total number of equal parts and the numerator for the selected parts.
The model is divided into four equal parts, and only one part is marked.
Select one part of the four equal parts, then submit the fraction represented by the model.
A point on a number line shows how far the amount is from zero.
Count the equal intervals from zero to the marked point and compare that count with the total intervals.
The marked point is at the first interval on a line divided into four equal intervals.
Read the point as one interval out of four, then submit the fraction in numerator-over-denominator form.
The denominator tells how many equal parts make one whole.
Read the requested unit in the question and use that number to divide the second line.
The question asks for eighths, so each part on Line 2 must be one eighth.
Enter the total number of equal eighth-sized intervals and press the confirmation control.
Equivalent fractions name the same position on the number line.
Transfer the location from Line 1 to Line 2 by counting equal intervals from zero.
Because each fourth is split into two eighths, the first fourth covers two eighth intervals.
Starting at zero, count the eighth intervals until you reach the marked point, then submit that location.
The numerator counts how many parts are selected.
Use the number of eighth intervals from zero to the marked point.
One fourth covers two parts when each fourth is divided into two smaller eighths.
Count the eighth intervals reached by the marked point and type that count in the numerator box.
Equivalent fractions describe the same quantity even when their numbers look different.
Compare the positions of the two fractions on the number lines.
The marked points coincide, so neither fraction is greater or smaller than the other.
Choose the symbol used when both sides have exactly the same value.
Before submitting, check that both fractions describe the same point.
Review the division of Line 2, the marked point, the numerator, and the comparison symbol.
Make sure Line 2 uses eighths and that the right-hand numerator matches the marked position.
When every part of the equivalence is complete, press the Done button to submit it.

exercicio.statement:
1/4 is marked on Line 1. Find another fraction that equals the same amount in eighths. Use Line 2 to find the answer.
One fourth equals how many eighths?

steps.instruction: Manipulate the fraction model to represent the marked amount as a fraction less than one.
Manipulate Line 1 to inspect the position marked at 1/4.
Enter the number of equal parts needed on Line 2, then confirm it.
Mark on Line 2 the point matching the position of 1/4 on Line 1.
Enter the numerator for the equivalent fraction in eighths.
Select the comparison symbol showing that the two fractions represent the same amount.
Click Done to submit the completed equivalent-fraction answer.

nodes.description: Inicio do exercicio
Exercicio completo
Manipulate the fraction model to represent the marked amount as a fraction less than one.
nodes.instruction: Manipulate the fraction model to represent the marked amount as a fraction less than one.

hints.message: A fraction less than one shows only part of one whole.
Use the denominator for the total number of equal parts and the numerator for the selected parts.
The model is divided into four equal parts, and only one part is marked.
Select one part of the four equal parts, then submit the fraction represented by the model.

nodes.description: Manipulate Line 1 to inspect the position marked at 1/4.
nodes.instruction: Manipulate Line 1 to inspect the position marked at 1/4.

hints.message: A point on a number line shows how far the amount is from zero.
Count the equal intervals from zero to the marked point and compare that count with the total intervals.
The marked point is at the first interval on a line divided into four equal intervals.
Read the point as one interval out of four, then submit the fraction in numerator-over-denominator form.

misconceptions.description: Aluno perde a referência visual e coloca o ponto na metade (4/8) por âncora cognitiva
misconceptions.feedback: The marked point is before the halfway point. One fourth is less than one half, so compare the point with the middle of the line.

misconceptions.description: Aluno começa a contar a partir do zero como 'primeira parte', marcando a posição anterior à correta
misconceptions.feedback: Start counting intervals after zero. The first interval ends at the first mark, not at zero.

misconceptions.description: Aluno interpreta mal a relação inversa e posiciona o ponto do lado oposto
misconceptions.feedback: The point is close to zero, not close to one. A smaller fraction lies nearer to zero on the number line.

nodes.description: Enter the number of equal parts needed on Line 2, then confirm it.
nodes.instruction: Enter the number of equal parts needed on Line 2, then confirm it.

hints.message: The denominator tells how many equal parts make one whole.
Read the requested unit in the question and use that number to divide the second line.
The question asks for eighths, so each part on Line 2 must be one eighth.
Enter the total number of equal eighth-sized intervals and press the confirmation control.

misconceptions.description: Aluno replica a divisão da reta de referência em vez de ajustar para o novo denominador solicitado
misconceptions.feedback: Line 1 uses fourths, but the new line must show eighths. Use the target denominator requested by the problem.

misconceptions.description: Aluno confunde número de marcas com número de partes, resultando em um a mais
misconceptions.feedback: Count the spaces between marks, not the marks themselves. Eight equal intervals represent eighths.

nodes.description: Mark on Line 2 the point matching the position of 1/4 on Line 1.
nodes.instruction: Mark on Line 2 the point matching the position of 1/4 on Line 1.

hints.message: Equivalent fractions name the same position on the number line.
Transfer the location from Line 1 to Line 2 by counting equal intervals from zero.
Because each fourth is split into two eighths, the first fourth covers two eighth intervals.
Starting at zero, count the eighth intervals until you reach the marked point, then submit that location.

misconceptions.description: Aluno perde a referência visual e coloca o ponto na metade (4/8) por âncora cognitiva
misconceptions.feedback: The halfway point is 4/8, but 1/4 is before halfway. Match the position of the point on Line 1.

misconceptions.description: Aluno começa a contar a partir do zero como 'primeira parte', marcando a posição anterior à correta
misconceptions.feedback: The first eighth ends at 1/8 and the second ends at the matching point. Count the intervals after zero carefully.

misconceptions.description: Aluno interpreta mal a relação inversa e posiciona o ponto do lado oposto
misconceptions.feedback: The point was placed too close to one. Since 1/4 is near zero, its equivalent point must also be near zero.

nodes.description: Enter the numerator for the equivalent fraction in eighths.
nodes.instruction: Enter the numerator for the equivalent fraction in eighths.

hints.message: The numerator counts how many parts are selected.
Use the number of eighth intervals from zero to the marked point.
One fourth covers two parts when each fourth is divided into two smaller eighths.
Count the eighth intervals reached by the marked point and type that count in the numerator box.

misconceptions.description: Aluno vê 'eighths' e responde '8', ignorando que o campo pede o numerador
misconceptions.feedback: The denominator 8 is already shown. The input asks for how many eighths reach the marked point.

misconceptions.description: Aluno acredita que o numerador permanece inalterado em frações equivalentes
misconceptions.feedback: The original numerator counts fourths. When the parts become eighths, one fourth is represented by two smaller parts.

nodes.description: Select the comparison symbol showing that the two fractions represent the same amount.
nodes.instruction: Select the comparison symbol showing that the two fractions represent the same amount.

hints.message: Equivalent fractions describe the same quantity even when their numbers look different.
Compare the positions of the two fractions on the number lines.
The marked points coincide, so neither fraction is greater or smaller than the other.
Choose the symbol used when both sides have exactly the same value.

nodes.description: Click Done to submit the completed equivalent-fraction answer.
nodes.instruction: Click Done to submit the completed equivalent-fraction answer.

hints.message: Before submitting, check that both fractions describe the same point.
Review the division of Line 2, the marked point, the numerator, and the comparison symbol.
Make sure Line 2 uses eighths and that the right-hand numerator matches the marked position.
When every part of the equivalence is complete, press the Done button to submit it.

nodes.instruction: Vamos retomar este passo. Identifique o conceito principal, divida o raciocínio em partes menores e tente novamente.
